subject: Dedicated capacity — follow-up: throughput, GPU preference & $/1M token targets
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@veridianlabs.com>, Priya Menon <priya@veridianlabs.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity — follow-up: throughput, GPU preference & $/1M token targets

Hi Sanjay / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can put together a dedicated-reservation proposal that matches Veridian's econ and latency targets.

Call highlights (my notes):
- Workload: multi-turn customer support + long-form summarization. Average generation lengths ~120 tokens; ~12% of requests are >512 tokens.
- Traffic profile: steady baseline with 3x traffic spikes during business hours; expected monthly growth ~10% for next 6 months.
- SLOs: P95 generation latency target ~400ms; soft P99 objective ~1.2s.
- Preferred GPUs: you mentioned H100 for latency but asked for cost check vs A100.
- Procurement timeline: target contract signed by end of Jan (you flagged procurement review in mid-Jan).

To build concrete pricing options we need two pieces from you (quick numbers will do):
1) Expected token volumes — please provide one of these: daily peak tokens, average daily tokens, or monthly tokens (tokens/month preferred).
2) Budget band — ballpark preferred $/1M tokens or monthly committed spend (we can show multiple tiers).

Proposed sizing questions for our side (we'll size a few options based on your answers):
- Reserved GPU count: would you prefer fewer H100s for latency or more A100s for unit cost? We can model both (e.g., 4x H100 vs 6x A100).
- Throughput target: what's a reasonable tokens/sec peak you'd like for the primary route?

Next steps: if you share the two items above, I’ll have a dedicated-reservation options deck + cost table (H100 vs A100, 3/6/12-month commits) ready for review in 48 hours. Attaching a draft pricing matrix (veridian_dedicated_pricing_v1.xlsx) with the variables we'll fill in.

Thanks — appreciate the clarity so we can avoid back-and-forth.

—Marcus

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@veridianlabs.com>

Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — follow-up: throughput, GPU preference & $/1M token targets

Marcus — thanks for the clear summary. See numbers below (rough but actionable):

Token volumes:
- Estimated steady-state: 20M tokens/day (includes user prompts + system tokens).
- Peak days: up to ~28–30M tokens/day during product launches (we expect those 2–4 times per quarter).
- Monthly baseline: ~600M tokens/month.

Budget target:
- Our procurement lens: ideally we target $800–$1,200 per 1M tokens for committed capacity (we know this will vary by commit length & GPU choice).

GPU preference / sizing:
- We prefer H100s for the latency-sensitive route (support chat) but open to a mixed topology — e.g., 3x H100 for low-latency + 4x A100 for batch/summary throughput.
- If you can show a straightforward comparison (4x H100 reserved vs 6x A100 reserved) with cost per 1M and expected P95s, that'd help our Eng + Procurement pick.

Throughput target:
- For the low-latency route: target 250–300k tokens/sec aggregate across the H100 pool during peak.

Procurement timeline: internal approval window mid-Jan; target PO by end of Jan if economics look reasonable.

--Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform, Veridian Labs
sanjay@veridianlabs.com

Folks — forwarding Veridian's reply (below). Key asks to action:
- Build two pricing options: (A) 4x H100 reserved + mixed pool for burst (B) 6x A100 reserved. Show $/1M tokens at 3/6/12-month commits and expected P95 latency numbers.
- Model bandwidth: low-latency pool must hit 250–300k tokens/sec during peak; show how autoscaling/burst would work and the cost of burst PR tokens beyond commit.
- Prepare a short slide (1–2 pages) with: recommended option, economics table tied to tokens/month, and procurement checklist (Docs we need for PO + SOC2 note).

Attached: internal pricing worksheet link (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-pricing-share). I started populating assumptions but will need Ben to validate kernel/sequence length cost multipliers.

Thanks — can we aim to have first-draft options Monday EOD (Dec 7)?

—Marcus

Sanjay / Priya — thanks again and appreciate the timeline. Attached is a short options packet + a draft Master Agreement (ma-draft-VER-9872.docx) to help procurement move faster. High-level options we will present:

Option 1 — Latency-first (recommended for chat-heavy front-line):
- 4x H100 reserved capacity (primary pool) + 2x A100 burst lane
- Modeled monthly tokens: 600M committed
- Modeled $/1M tokens: $950 (3-month commit), $880 (6-month), $820 (12-month) — final numbers will be detailed in the deck.
- Expected P95: ~380–420ms for typical 120-token responses; P99 ~1.0–1.3s depending on sequence lengths.

Option 2 — Cost-first (higher token throughput per $):
- 6x A100 reserved capacity (single pool) with H100s for small low-latency tier if needed
- Modeled $/1M tokens: $780 (3m), $720 (6m), $680 (12m)
- Expected P95: ~650–800ms for same payloads.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm which option to deep-dive (latency vs cost) and your preferred commit length (3/6/12 months)?
- If Veridian confirms an option, we'll produce a finalized quote + procurement packet (SOC2 report, network diagram, PO instructions) by EOD two business days after confirmation.
- Proposed 30-min sync: Monday Dec 8, 11:00–11:30 PT — bookable if that works for you.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/VER-9872).

Thanks — attaching the decks and MA draft for procurement review.

—Marcus
